text.p: Britain's Guinness Plc said on Wendesday its directors unanimously accepted the resignation of the Bernard Arnault, the rebel chairman of French shareholder LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton.

"It was the unanimous view of the directors that it was appropriate for Mr. Arnault to leave the board given his conflict of interest in representing the shareholders of both Guinness and LVMH," Guinness said in a brief statement.
Arnault had been a Guinness director since March 1989.

The French luxury goods group has fiercely opposed a planned 24 billion stg merger between Guinness and food and drinks group Grand Metropolitan which threatens to sideline LVMH -- although the company is the largest shareholder in both companies.

Under the formidable and tenacious leadership of Arnault, LVMH has been raising its GrandMet stake in an effort to force the two British partners to agree to its own plan for a three-way drinks combination. Other businesses would be sold off.
Arnault quit the Guinness board two days ago amid a lack of managerial support for his plans which, he says, offer "significantly greater value for all shareholders."
Analysts say Arnault has more firepower with a lower stake in GrandMet than with Guinness. The resignation will allow him to focus on gathering support for and promoting his alternative proposal.

In an effort to increase its leverage over the planned merger, LVMH has been buying bought GrandMet shares and selling some of its 14.2 percent Guinness stake. Sources and analysts say the French company was likely to control more than 10 percent and aim for 15 percent.

With a 10 percent stake, LVMH can call an extraordinary general meeting and if it wins enough allies to form a 25 percent block, it could force the multi-billion pound merger, that was announced in May, to be abandoned.

LVMH has declined to comment on reports that Arnault was travelling to Britain this week to try to convince Guinness and GrandMet shareholders that his plan would generate more value than the creation of a sprawling drinks, beer, canned goods and fast foods conglomerate.
